statement: Ten different positive whole numbers add up to 75. What is the largest value the biggest of them can have?

choices.misconception: I made the other nine numbers all equal to 1, forgetting the numbers must be different.
I let the nine smaller numbers be 0 to 8, but 0 is not a positive number.
I subtracted 1 + 2 + ... + 10 from 75, which wrongly includes a tenth small number.
I found the smallest the biggest number can be, not the largest.

hints: To make one number big, make the rest small.
The biggest number is largest when the other nine take up as little of the total as possible. Find the smallest possible sum of nine different positive whole numbers.
The nine smallest different positive whole numbers are 1 to 9, which add to 45.

solutions.reliable: The other nine numbers are different positive whole numbers, so their sum is at least 1 + 2 + ... + 9 = 45. Then the biggest is at most 75 - 45 = 30, and 1, 2, ..., 9, 30 shows that 30 is reached. The transferable idea: to push one quantity to an extreme, push everything else to the opposite extreme, then check the extreme case is allowed.

whyOnTest: Extremal questions reward pushing every other quantity to its limit, and the trap is breaking one of the stated conditions while doing it.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
